lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Transfer challenge: proving the Law of Sines

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different context than the problems below.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A triangle problem gives two angles and any side (AAS or ASA). Which law should be used first?
choices: the law of sines, with a check for the ambiguous case

items.prompt: In a triangle, sides a = 3 and b = 14 enclose an angle C = 120°. Find c², the square of the third side.
In a triangle, angle A = 45°, angle B = 68°, and side a = 11 (opposite A). Find side b to two decimal places.
A triangle has sides a = 30 and b = 13 enclosing an angle of 30°. Find its area exactly.
A triangle problem gives all three sides (SSS). Which law should be used first?
choices: the law of sines, with a check for the ambiguous case

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: These are meant to be hard. Show the reasoning even if you do not finish.

items.prompt: In a triangle, sides a = 2 and b = 13 enclose an angle C = 120°. Find c², the square of the third side.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: In a triangle, angle A = 39°, angle B = 82°, and side a = 25 (opposite A). Find side b to two decimal places.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A triangle has sides a = 4 and b = 8 enclosing an angle of 30°. Find its area exactly.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
